advertised_routes.description: List of IP Prefixes that will be advertised to the remote provider. Both IPv4 and IPv6 addresses are supported.
advertised_routes.rationale: Controls which IP prefixes are advertised to the remote provider. Overly broad or unauthorized route advertisements can expose unintended internal networks, so advertised prefixes should be restricted to approved ranges.

bandwidth.description: Bandwidth of the Transport. This must be one of the supported bandwidths for the remote profile.
bandwidth.rationale: Controls transport capacity and performance but does not directly determine network trust, routing authorization, or access.

deletion_policy.description:
Whether Terraform will be prevented from destroying the instance. Defaults to "DELETE".
When a 'terraform destroy' or 'terraform apply' would delete the instance,
the command will fail if this field is set to "PREVENT" in Terraform state.
When set to "ABANDON", the command will remove the resource from Terraform
management without updating or deleting the resource in the API.
When set to "DELETE", deleting the resource is allowed.
deletion_policy.rationale: Prevents accidental or unauthorized Terraform destruction of critical transport infrastructure. A policy should require the deletion-blocking value PREVENT.

description.description: An optional description of this resource.
description.rationale: Provides descriptive metadata only and does not directly affect connectivity, routing, or access.

labels.description:
Optional labels in key:value format. For more information about labels, see [Requirements for labels](https://cloud.google.com/resource-manager/docs/creating-managing-labels#requirements).

**Note**: This field is non-authoritative, and will only manage the labels present in your configuration.
Please refer to the field 'effective_labels' for all of the labels present on the resource.
labels.rationale: Labels provide resource metadata and governance information but do not directly control transport connectivity, routing, or traffic flow.

mtu_limit.description: [Output only] The maximum transmission unit (MTU) of a packet that can be sent over this transport.
mtu_limit.rationale: This is an output-only value describing the maximum packet size and is not a user-controlled security configuration.

name.description: Name of the resource, see google.aip.dev/122 for resource naming.
name.rationale: Identifies the Transport resource but does not directly control connectivity, route advertisement, or remote access.

network.description: Resource URL of the Network that will be peered with this Transport. This field must be provided during resource creation and cannot be changed.
network.rationale: References the VPC network peered with the Transport. It is a resource-reference argument and cannot be generically constrained without hardcoding organization-specific resource names.

project.description: The ID of the project in which the resource belongs. If it is not provided, the provider project is used.
project.rationale: Determines resource ownership and governance scope, but without an explicit organization-specific approved-project requirement it does not need a standalone security policy.

provided_activation_key.description: Key used for establishing a connection with the remote transport. This key can only be provided if the profile supports an INPUT key flow and the resource is in the PENDING_KEY state.
provided_activation_key.rationale: Contains sensitive connection material used to establish the remote transport. Policy should prevent plaintext or hardcoded secret exposure and require approved secret-handling practices.

region.description: The region of this resource. This is required to construct the resource name, but is not sent to the API since the region is already contained in the parent field.
region.rationale: Determines the region where the Transport is created. Restricting deployment to approved regions supports data residency and controlled infrastructure placement.

remote_account_id.description: The user supplied account id for the CSP associated with the remote profile.
remote_account_id.rationale: Identifies an external provider account. It is an organization-specific external reference and cannot be generalized into a platform policy without hardcoding tenant-specific values.

remote_profile.description:
Resource URL of the remoteTransportProfile that this Transport is
connecting to.
remote_profile.rationale: Selects a remote transport profile and therefore an architectural connectivity type. The referenced resource name is not inherently secure or insecure and should not be hardcoded in generic policy.

stack_type.description: IP version stack for the established connectivity. Possible values: ["IPV4_IPV6", "IPV4_ONLY"]
stack_type.rationale: Selects IPv4-only or dual-stack connectivity. The appropriate value depends on network architecture and neither option is inherently insecure, so no generic standalone security policy is required.
